newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seen pausing next week after records.
newsitem.headline: German shares seen pausing next week after records.

text.p: German shares, drawing breath after a week of record highs, were expected to start next week in more tentative form, dealers said on Friday.
The blue chip DAX index chalked up gains of three percent this week, chasing Wall Street to an all-time high of 3,612.46 points during IBIS electronic dealings on Tuesday.

On Friday, the IBIS DAX was up 15.55 points at 3,553.00 points at 1252 GMT as firm Bunds and a relatively stable dollar buoyed a mainly thinly traded market. The DAX ended bourse trade somewhat firmer, at 3,562.41 points.
June DTB DAX futures were up 8.0 points at 3,555.0

"In the short term the market appears overbought after the steep rise of the past weeks, so that it would be advisable for flexible investors to take profits at the current level or secure their positions," Bayerische Vereinsbank's research team said.

Nonetheless, mid-term prospects for a further assault on all-time highs were generally viewed as good, and some dealers said they expected the DAX to be back around the 3,600 level by the end of next week.
But on Friday afternoon, investor activity, apart from in selected shares such as Siemens AG, was close to nil.

Siemens surged for the first time past a crucial technical threshold of 100 marks to trade up 2.38 marks at 100.85 in post-bourse dealings, boosted by news of an Auckland power station contract and by a well-received investor presentation, dealers said.
Software firm SAP AG, in the limelight this week after a probe began into alleged insider dealing in its shares, was up two percent at 324.65 marks as it traded ex-dividend.
Airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG, in vogue after earlier this week revealing its first ever first-quarter profit, led the field with gains of 3.78 percent, at 28 marks.
Trinkaus Capital Management said the airline's shares could reach 30 marks in the mid-term.
